# Draft:World Traditional Taekwondo Federation (GTTF)

----
The Global Traditional Taekwondo Federation (GTTF) is an international nonprofit organization dedicated to preserving and promoting Traditional Taekwondo. Established in 2023, the federation emphasizes the martial art’s classical forms, ethical teachings, and philosophical roots, distinguishing itself from modern sport-oriented Taekwondo practices.
.
Background
Traditional Taekwondo refers to the foundational martial art system that emerged in Korea in the mid-20th century, drawing from older Korean martial traditions such as Taekkyeon and Hwa Rang Do, as well as influences from Japanese and Chinese martial arts. While Taekwondo has evolved in multiple directions, Traditional Taekwondo is often associated with the pre-Olympic era of the 1950s–1970s, when it was taught primarily as a method of self-defense, character development, and ethical discipline.
The practice is structured around five primary components:
Poomsae (forms): Pre-arranged sequences of techniques that build muscle memory and express philosophical principles.
Kyorugi (sparring): Controlled partner-based combat emphasizing timing, distance, and respect.
Ho-sin-sool (self-defense): Practical defense techniques against grabs, strikes, or weapons.
Kyukpa (breaking): The application of technique and power against inanimate targets such as boards or tiles.
Do-deok (ethics/morality): Study and practice of virtues like integrity, perseverance, and respect.
Traditional Taekwondo places strong emphasis on mental discipline, cultural etiquette, and personal growth, often prioritizing these over competitive success. Training takes place in a dojang (training hall), where students wear dobok uniforms, train barefoot, and follow a structured hierarchy with strict behavioral codes.
History
The GTTF was officially founded on May 16, 2023, by a coalition of Taekwondo masters concerned about the diminishing presence of traditional values in modern martial arts instruction. On September 12, 2024, it was legally registered as a nonprofit organization in North Carolina, United States, and recognized by the Internal Revenue Service as a charitable entity.
The federation emerged in reaction to the global rise of Sport Taekwondo, particularly as governed by World Taekwondo (WT), which is oriented around Olympic-style competition. While Sport Taekwondo emphasizes speed, agility, and point-based sparring under strict rules, traditionalists expressed concern over what they viewed as a loss of martial discipline, etiquette, and philosophical depth.
Founding members included practitioners and instructors from several countries who sought to return Taekwondo to its foundational principles. These founders included Oskar Posada, Sergio Chavez, Jun Lee, Varo Barragan, Nelson Brizuela, and Abhai Singh Rathore.
Global Scope
The GTTF operates through affiliated dojangs and regional coordinators worldwide. Its organizational hubs include:
* North America Headquarters: Raleigh, North Carolina, USA
* Asia Regional Office: Gwangmyeong, South Korea
The federation supports local Taekwondo schools, organizes seminars, and hosts educational initiatives to reinforce traditional martial arts training.
Vision and Philosophy
The Global Traditional Taekwondo Federation (GTTF) promotes Taekwondo as a comprehensive martial discipline that integrates physical conditioning, self-defense, mental focus, and ethical development. The federation views Taekwondo not solely as a combat technique but as a lifelong path to personal growth and social contribution.
GTTF emphasizes:
* The preservation of classical techniques, forms (poomsae), and terminology rooted in traditional Taekwondo practice.
* The revival of traditional etiquette, particularly the role of instructors as moral exemplars and educators rather than merely athletic coaches.
* The promotion of Taekwondo as a cultural art form that reflects Korean heritage and martial values.
GTTF also offers structured programs designed to educate new generations of practitioners on these traditional principles, regardless of age or competitive goals.
Certification
GTTF issues its own Poom and Dan certifications to members who complete practical and theoretical examinations under the federation’s guidelines. Certification is conducted through official regional representatives. The federation recognizes Kukkiwon credentials and facilitates access to them through its internal processes.
Membership and Reach
As of June 2025, GTTF reports having affiliated members and representatives in over 160 countries. Its operations include training programs, events, and technical development workshops aligned with its traditional focus.
Media and Public Reception
The Global Traditional Taekwondo Federation (GTTF) has received media attention in both national and international outlets. Articles and coverage have highlighted its leadership’s global outreach and its emphasis on traditional Taekwondo’s cultural and ethical significance.
The GTTF has been featured in various international media outlets, which have reported on its activities, leadership, and global expansion:
* On September 27, 2023, Korea Mooye News published an article introducing GTTF and its goals of preserving traditional Taekwondo. [https://www.mooye.net/22083](https://www.mooye.net/22083)
* On October 18, 2024, South Korean media covered GTTF’s organizational developments and its recognition in the Taekwondo community. [https://news.nate.com/view/20241018n03389](https://news.nate.com/view/20241018n03389)
* On November 19, 2024, Money Today Korea reported on GTTF’s engagement with global martial arts institutions. [https://news.mt.co.kr/mtview.php?no=2024111818012146731](https://news.mt.co.kr/mtview.php?no=2024111818012146731)
* On March 26, 2025, the Italian news portal Magazin Plus reported on Grand Master Jun Lee’s visit to Bosnia and his mission to promote traditional Taekwondo. [https://magazinplus.eu/grand-master-jun-lee-stigao-u-bih/](https://magazinplus.eu/grand-master-jun-lee-stigao-u-bih/)
* On April 2, 2025, Trend.com.hr (Croatia) featured an article on Jun Lee’s arrival in Karlovac and his meetings with prominent Taekwondo figures. [https://trend.com.hr/2025/04/02/jun-lee-stigao-u-karlovac-ugostili-ga-zasluzni-njegovatelji-taekwondo-vjestine-i-sporta/](https://trend.com.hr/2025/04/02/jun-lee-stigao-u-karlovac-ugostili-ga-zasluzni-njegovatelji-taekwondo-vjestine-i-sporta/)
* On April 3, 2025, KAportal published coverage of Jun Lee’s impressions of Taekwondo achievements in Karlovac since 1968. [https://kaportal.net.hr/kas/1352234/taekwondo-velemajstor-jun-lee-u-posjeti-karlovcu-impresioniran-postignutim-rezultatima-od-1968-godine-do-danas/](https://kaportal.net.hr/kas/1352234/taekwondo-velemajstor-jun-lee-u-posjeti-karlovcu-impresioniran-postignutim-rezultatima-od-1968-godine-do-danas/)
* On April 18 and April 22, 2025, Travels Dubai published interviews with Jun Lee, highlighting his global campaign to revive traditional Taekwondo:
* [April 18 article](https://www.travelsdubai.com/18-Apr-2025/watch-grand-master-jun-lee-on-a-mission-to-revive-traditional-taekwondo)
* [April 22 article](https://www.travelsdubai.com/22-Apr-2025/grand-master-jun-lee-on-a-mission-to-revive-traditional-taekwondo)
* On April 30, 2025, Forsan Sports in Saudi Arabia covered GTTF’s activities and interest in expanding to the Middle East. [https://forsansports.com/?p=117048](https://forsansports.com/?p=117048)
* In April 2025, Al Ghad (Jordan) published a feature on the federation’s regional cooperation and events. [https://alghad.com/story/1999737](https://alghad.com/story/1999737)
* On June 2, 2025, the well-known martial arts magazine MasTKD described GTTF as “the federation reviving the traditional spirit of Taekwondo” in a detailed article. [https://www.mastkd.com/2025/06/gttf-la-federacion-que-rescata-el-espiritu-tradicional-del-taekwondo/](https://www.mastkd.com/2025/06/gttf-la-federacion-que-rescata-el-espiritu-tradicional-del-taekwondo/)
President Jun Lee’s international visits have also been profiled, particularly his campaigns to engage traditional martial arts communities in Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.
Notable Members
Several individuals affiliated with the GTTF have distinguished themselves in various fields:
* Samer Kamal – Olympic bronze medalist, 1988 Seoul Games (Jordan)
* Manuel Jurado – Olympic bronze medalist, 1988 Seoul Games (Mexico)
* Herbert Perez – Olympic gold medalist, 1992 Barcelona Games (USA)
* Yumnam Khemchand Singh – Government minister, Manipur, India
* Srishti Rana – Miss Asia Pacific World 2013
* Salvador Carrillo Vázquez – 2014 World Poomsae Championship medalist
* Violeta Chávez – Multi-medalist in Pan American and international Poomsae events
* Jaime De Pablos – Silver medalist, World Taekwondo Championships (1975, 1977, 1979)
Organizational Structure
As of 2025, the GTTF’s leadership includes:
* Chairperson: Moon Ki Ju
* President: Jun Lee
* Secretary General: Fernando Abaga
* Head of Operations (USA): Jun Lee
The Council includes:
* Samer Kamal
* Norbert Mosch
* Oskar Posada
* Sergio Chavez
* Nelson Brizuela
* Abhai Singh Rathore
* Varo Barragan
